review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

18:1.sourceText: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Τίς ἄρα μείζων ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν;
18:1.targetText: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

groups.note: The comparative μείζων (greater) is rendered as the English superlative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle λέγοντες (saying) is rendered as the finite verb asked.

18:2.sourceText: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν
18:2.targetText: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.

groups.note: The participle προσκαλεσάμενος (having called to himself) is rendered as the main verb.
The transitive ἔστησεν (he set) is recast as the infinitive after invited.
ἐν μέσῳ (in the midst of) is rendered among.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening connective is not rendered in English.
The object pronoun αὐτό (him) is not repeated; English makes the child the subject of to stand.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb ending.

18:3.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ στραφῆτε καὶ γένησθε ὡς τὰ παιδία, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
18:3.targetText: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

groups.note: οὐ μή is an emphatic double negative.
The aorist subjunctive under οὐ μή is rendered as an English future.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective before He said is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.

18:4.sourceText: ὅστις οὖν ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὡς τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μείζων ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
18:4.targetText: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive οὗτος (this one) is not repeated in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:5.sourceText: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται ἓν παιδίον τοιοῦτο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται·
18:5.targetText: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:6.sourceText: ὃς δ’ ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἵνα κρεμασθῇ μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης.
18:6.targetText: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.

groups.note: The indefinite relative ὃς ἄν (whoever) is rendered as a condition.
ἵνα with the subjunctive is rendered as an English infinitive.
The passive κρεμασθῇ (be hung) is rendered have ... hung.
ὀνικός (of a donkey) marks a millstone turned by a donkey, rendered large.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:7.sourceText: Οὐαὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀπὸ τῶν σκανδάλων· ἀνάγκη γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τὰ σκάνδαλα, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ δι’ οὗ τὸ σκάνδαλον ἔρχεται.
18:7.targetText: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!

groups.note: ἀνάγκη (necessity) with the infinitive is rendered must.
The anaphoric article is rendered These.
The singular σκάνδαλον (stumbling block) is rendered by the pronoun they.

unmappedSource.reason: The explanatory γάρ (for) is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:8.sourceText: Εἰ δὲ ἡ χείρ σου ἢ ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν, ἢ δύο χεῖρας ἢ δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον.
18:8.targetText: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

groups.note: σκανδαλίζει (causes to stumble) is rendered causes ... to sin.
The one pronoun is the object of both cut off and throw away.
ἀπὸ σοῦ (from you) is rendered away.
BSB renders ἢ (or) as and in this list.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; Greek joins the participle ἔχοντα (having) to βληθῆναι without a conjunction.

18:9.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
18:9.targetText: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.

groups.note: The one pronoun is the object of both gouge out and throw away.
ἀπὸ σοῦ (from you) is rendered away.
BSB reverses τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός (the Gehenna of fire) to the fire of hell.

unmappedSource.reason: The preposition repeats the verb's prefix and is absorbed in English enter.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; Greek joins the participle ἔχοντα (having) to βληθῆναι without a conjunction.

18:10.sourceText: Ὁρᾶτε μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων· λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
18:10.targetText: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.

groups.note: After a verb of warning, μή means that ... not (lest).
διὰ παντός (through all [time]) is rendered always.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:12.sourceText: Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; ἐὰν γένηταί τινι ἀνθρώπῳ ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ πλανηθῇ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν, οὐχὶ ἀφήσει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη καὶ πορευθεὶς ζητεῖ τὸ πλανώμενον;
18:12.targetText: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?

groups.note: The impersonal Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ (what does it seem to you) is recast with you as subject.
γένηται with the dative (there be to a man) is rendered has.

18:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν γένηται εὑρεῖν αὐτό, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι χαίρει ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τοῖς μὴ πεπλανημένοις.
18:13.targetText: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.

groups.note: γένηται εὑρεῖν (it happens that he finds) is rendered he finds.
The pronoun αὐτῷ (it) is rendered that one.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι (that) after I tell you is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the noun; the Greek has only the pronoun αὐτῷ.

18:14.sourceText: οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν θέλημα ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μικρῶν τούτων.
18:14.targetText: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.

groups.note: The noun θέλημα (will) is rendered by the adjective willing.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes Father the subject, so ἔμπροσθεν (before) has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:15.sourceText: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου, ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου. ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ, ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου·
18:15.targetText: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.

groups.note: μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου (between you and him alone) is rendered privately.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; Greek sets the imperatives ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον (go, confront) side by side.
BSB follows a reading with εἰς σέ (against you), which N1904 lacks.

18:16.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀκούσῃ, παράλαβε μετὰ σοῦ ἔτι ἕνα ἢ δύο, ἵνα ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα·
18:16.targetText: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’

groups.note: μετὰ σοῦ (with you) is rendered along.
ἔτι (besides, more) is rendered others.
στόματος (mouth) is rendered the testimony.

18:17.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ παρακούσῃ αὐτῶν, εἰπὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας παρακούσῃ, ἔστω σοι ὥσπερ ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης.
18:17.targetText: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

groups.note: ἔστω σοι (let him be to you) is recast as regard him ... as you would.
The generic article is rendered a.
BSB renders καί (and) as or.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of tell; the Greek has none.

18:18.sourceText: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅσα ἐὰν δήσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ.
18:18.targetText: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:19.sourceText: Πάλιν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς περὶ παντὸς πράγματος οὗ ἐὰν αἰτήσωνται, γενήσεται αὐτοῖς παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
18:19.targetText: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.

groups.note: παντὸς πράγματος (every matter) is rendered anything.
BSB renders the third-person plural (they ask) as you ask.
αὐτοῖς (for them) is rendered for you.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative οὗ ἐάν (whatever) is left implicit in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:20.sourceText: οὗ γάρ εἰσιν δύο ἢ τρεῖς συνηγμένοι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα, ἐκεῖ εἰμι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν.
18:20.targetText: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”

groups.note: The periphrastic εἰσιν συνηγμένοι (are gathered) is rendered gather together.
ἐν μέσῳ (in the midst of) is rendered with.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:21.sourceText: Τότε προσελθὼν ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Κύριε, ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ; ἕως ἑπτάκις;
18:21.targetText: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτῷ (to him) is rendered to Jesus.
ἀδελφός (subject of sins) and αὐτῷ (him, object of forgive) both refer to the brother, named once in English.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, naming or noun construction.
BSB recasts the two clauses as forgive my brother who sins, so καί (and) is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle προσελθών is rendered as the finite verb came.

18:22.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις, ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά.
18:22.targetText: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!

groups.note: ἕως (up to) is rendered just.
BSB reads ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά as seventy-seven times; it can also mean seventy times seven.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ (to him) is not rendered.
The second ἕως (up to) is not rendered again.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:23.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὃς ἠθέλησεν συνᾶραι λόγον μετὰ τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ.
18:23.targetText: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the apposition ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ (a man, a king) simply as a king.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:24.sourceText: ἀρξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ συναίρειν προσήχθη εἷς αὐτῷ ὀφειλέτης μυρίων ταλάντων.
18:24.targetText: As he began the settlements, a debtor was brought to him owing ten thousand talents.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἀρξαμένου αὐτοῦ (as he began) supplies As.
The infinitive συναίρειν (to settle accounts) is rendered the settlements.
ὀφειλέτης with a genitive (debtor of) is rendered debtor ... owing.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.

18:25.sourceText: μὴ ἔχοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποδοῦναι ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει, καὶ ἀποδοθῆναι.
18:25.targetText: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.

groups.note: The genitive absolute μὴ ἔχοντος (not having the means) supplies Since and was unable.
The pronoun αὐτοῦ (he) is rendered the man.
The article is rendered as the possessive his.
The passive infinitive ἀποδοθῆναι (to be repaid) is rendered as purpose, to pay.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The relative ὅσα (as much as) is left implicit in English.
The connective before the last infinitive is not rendered; English makes it a purpose clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the complementizer; Greek has ἐκέλευσεν with an accusative and infinitive.
English supplies the object of pay; the Greek passive infinitive has none.

18:26.sourceText: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ δοῦλος προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί, καὶ πάντα ἀποδώσω σοι.
18:26.targetText: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’

groups.note: προσεκύνει (bowed down, did homage) is rendered on his knees.
The participle λέγων (saying) is rendered he begged.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object σοι (to you) is not rendered.

18:27.sourceText: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ.
18:27.targetText: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.

groups.note: τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου (of that servant) is rendered His.
The dative αὐτῷ (forgave him the loan) is rendered as the possessive his.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of compassion; the Greek participle has none.

18:28.sourceText: ἐξελθὼν δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος εὗρεν ἕνα τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ, ὃς ὤφειλεν αὐτῷ ἑκατὸν δηνάρια, καὶ κρατήσας αὐτὸν ἔπνιγεν λέγων Ἀπόδος εἴ τι ὀφείλεις.
18:28.targetText: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’

groups.note: The participle ἐξελθών (having gone out) supplies the when clause.
The genitive article marks the partitive one of.
The one object pronoun serves both grabbed and choke.
The imperfect ἔπνιγεν is rendered as inceptive began to choke.
εἴ τι (if anything) is rendered what.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered; English begins a new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle κρατήσας is rendered as the finite verb grabbed.
English supplies me; N1904 has no pronoun (some manuscripts add μοι after Ἀπόδος).

18:29.sourceText: πεσὼν οὖν ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί, καὶ ἀποδώσω σοι.
18:29.targetText: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων (saying) is represented by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle πεσών is rendered as the finite verb fell down.

18:30.sourceText: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς φυλακὴν ἕως ἀποδῷ τὸ ὀφειλόμενον.
18:30.targetText: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.

groups.note: The article ὁ with δέ serves as the pronoun he.
οὐκ ἤθελεν (was not willing) is rendered refused.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered the man.
τὸ ὀφειλόμενον (what was owed) is rendered his debt.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀπελθών is rendered as the finite verb went.

18:31.sourceText: ἰδόντες οὖν οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ γενόμενα ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα, καὶ ἐλθόντες διεσάφησαν τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν πάντα τὰ γενόμενα.
18:31.targetText: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.

groups.note: The participle ἰδόντες (having seen) supplies the When clause.
τὰ γενόμενα (the things that had happened) is rendered this.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐλθόντες is rendered as the finite verb went.

18:32.sourceText: τότε προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ Δοῦλε πονηρέ, πᾶσαν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἐκείνην ἀφῆκά σοι, ἐπεὶ παρεκάλεσάς με·
18:32.targetText: Then the master summoned him and declared, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.

groups.note: The historic present λέγει (says) is rendered declared.
The dative σοι (forgave you) is rendered as the possessive your.

unmappedSource.reason: The possessive αὐτοῦ (his) is not rendered; BSB has the master.
The indirect object αὐτῷ (to him) is not rendered.
The demonstrative ἐκείνην (that) is not rendered; BSB has your debt.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle προσκαλεσάμενος is rendered as the finite verb summoned.

18:33.sourceText: οὐκ ἔδει καὶ σὲ ἐλεῆσαι τὸν σύνδουλόν σου, ὡς κἀγὼ σὲ ἠλέησα;
18:33.targetText: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’

groups.note: οὐκ ἔδει (was it not necessary) is rendered Shouldn’t.
κἀγώ (I also) is rendered I.
English repeats had ... on for the second verb of mercy; mercy itself is not repeated.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί (also) is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:34.sourceText: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν τοῖς βασανισταῖς ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ πᾶν τὸ ὀφειλόμενον αὐτῷ.
18:34.targetText: In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.

groups.note: βασανισταί (torturers) is rendered jailers ... to be tortured.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective is not rendered in English.
The dative αὐτῷ (to him, the master) is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

18:35.sourceText: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ποιήσει ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ἀφῆτε ἕκαστος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν.
18:35.targetText: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”

groups.note: ἕκαστος (each), the subject of forgive in Greek, is moved to each of you.
αὐτοῦ (his) is rendered your to match you forgive.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί (also) is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
